answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so influence decays when transitions repeatedly encounter a sparse boundary. A sybil cluster is therefore a low-conductance cut: few attestations connect it to honest nodes, limiting stationary mass and aggregate voting weight for honest-seeded walks. Spectral-gap and min-cut transitivity bounds make this limit explicit, even when identities wander through tundra, willow, or other aliases.
